title: Data Product Operating Framework
description: One universal operating model for directing, defining, operating and assuring data products, with enterprise and AI-agent-first implementation profiles.

chapters.title: Start Here: Implement One Complete Data Product Chain

context.title: One reviewable chain
context.summary: The pilot proves one decision path before a broader operating-model rollout is considered.

panels.label: Minimum pilot chain
panels.code:
objective → use case → product decision
→ ODPS contract → catalog reference
→ relationship graph → validation workflow
→ runtime observation → value review

panels.label: End-of-pilot review
panels.code:
review:
  product: discoverable and governed
  access: appropriate for the use case
  commitment: observed, not assumed
  outcome: compared with baseline
  decision: continue, change or stop

details.label: Scope
details.value: One decision and one product extension

details.label: Evidence
details.value: Declared state, observed state and review record

context.title: One chain across four functions
context.summary: The same product decision remains traceable as it moves from demand to definition, operation and assurance.

panels.label: Function hand-offs
panels.code:
DIRECT  → objective, use case, investment
DEFINE  → contract, semantics, commitments
OPERATE → catalog, access, workflow
ASSURE  → observation, controls, value review

context.title: Read by evidence path
context.summary: Use the capability pages to find the decision, minimum practice and evidence required at each point in the chain.

panels.label: Reading route
panels.code:
1. Name the decision
2. Find the applicable capability
3. Record declared state
4. Collect operating evidence
5. Review the next decision

context.title: Owned churn objective
context.summary: The retention director owns a measurable objective before any product extension is funded.

example.label: Objective record
example.code:
objective:
  id: OBJ-REDUCE-CHURN
  metric: annual_churn
  baseline: 18 percent
  target: 14 percent by 2027
  owner: Retention Director

chapters.title: C2 Demand and Use Case Management
chapters.navLabel: C2 Demand and Use Case Management

context.title: 30-day churn-risk use case
context.summary: The team starts with the retention decision and information need, not a request for a new dashboard or product.

example.label: Use-case record
example.code:
use_case:
  id: UC-CHURN-RISK-30D
  decision: approve retention intervention
  horizon: 30 days
  needs: [purchases, service interactions, loyalty]
  gap: service interactions

context.title: Extend, do not duplicate
context.summary: The portfolio board funds a service-interaction extension to the existing product instead of a churn-only duplicate.

example.label: Portfolio decision
example.code:
decision:
  action: extend
  product: Customer 360
  reject: churn-risk duplicate
  accountable_team: Customer Data Products
  value_review: six months after adoption

context.title: Authoritative contract
context.summary: The extension is represented by a schema-valid ODPS 4.2 contract rather than a catalog-only description.

example.label: ODPS contract excerpt
example.code:
product:
  details:
    en:
      productID: customer-360
      productVersion: '2.4.0'
      visibility: restricted

context.title: Shared retention terms
context.summary: Customer and service interaction have governed definitions so consumers and agents do not infer their own meaning.

example.label: ODPV term excerpt
example.code:
term:
  id: ServiceInteraction
  preferredLabel: Service interaction
  definition: approved assisted customer contact
  usedIn: [ODPS, ODPC, ODPG]

chapters.title: C6 Product Commitments and Usage Conditions
chapters.navLabel: C6 Product Commitments and Usage Conditions

context.title: Declared commitments
context.summary: The scenario separates tested expectations from later runtime evidence and keeps human release approval explicit.

example.label: Declared service state
example.code:
commitments:
  completeness: '>= 98 percent'
  freshness: '<= 60 minutes'
  availability: '>= 99.9 percent'
  release_approval: human required

context.title: Traceable value path
context.summary: The graph connects the churn objective, use case, product, access policy and release workflow.

example.label: ODPG relationship excerpt

context.title: Discovery reference
context.summary: The catalog exposes the use case and product reference while pointing back to the authoritative ODPS contract.

example.label: ODPC catalog excerpt
example.code:
productReference:
  productID: customer-360
  productVersion: '2.4.0'
  visibility: restricted
  productModel: { standard: ODPS, format: yaml }

context.title: Controlled retention access
context.summary: The access decision ties the retention group, permitted use and product version together before consumption begins.

example.label: Access decision
example.code:
access_decision:
  consumer: Retention Analytics
  use_case: UC-CHURN-RISK-30D
  product: Customer 360 2.4.0
  permission: approved read access

chapters.title: C10 Lifecycle, Version and Change Management
chapters.navLabel: C10 Lifecycle, Version and Change Management

context.title: Version drift found
context.summary: The declared contract is 2.4.0 while the observed production version is 2.3.0, so the release state needs reconciliation.

example.label: Version reconciliation
example.code:
version_check:
  declared: '2.4.0'
  observed: '2.3.0'
  status: failed
  required_action: reconcile before release

chapters.title: C11 Workflow, Automation and Agent Operations
chapters.navLabel: C11 Workflow, Automation and Agent Operations

context.title: Release validation workflow
context.summary: A portable recipe validates the contract and graph before the separate human production-approval gate.

example.label: ODPR recipe excerpt
example.code:
steps:
  - command: validate
    document: product.odps.yaml
  - command: validate
    document: relationships.odpg.yaml
  - gate: human production approval

context.title: Completeness failed
context.summary: Freshness and availability pass, but 94.7% completeness fails the declared 98% threshold and triggers remediation.

example.label: Runtime observation

chapters.title: C13 Governance, Risk, Compliance and Control Assurance
chapters.navLabel: C13 Governance, Risk, Compliance and Control Assurance

context.title: Control findings
context.summary: An unresolved entitlement and a missing latest-deployment approval are findings until a valid exception exists.

example.label: Control evidence
example.code:
findings:
  - control: approved consumers only
    observed: one unresolved entitlement
  - control: human release approval
    observed: latest-deployment record missing
  status: open

chapters.title: C14 Adoption, Outcomes and Value Realisation
chapters.navLabel: C14 Adoption, Outcomes and Value Realisation

context.title: Value review
context.summary: The retention workflow adopted the extension, but churn moved only to 17.2%; the review records cost and confounding factors before the next decision.

example.label: Six-month value review
example.code:
value_review:
  adopted_workflow: churn-risk intervention
  churn: { baseline: '18%', observed: '17.2%', target: '14%' }
  confounders: [other campaigns, seasonality, completeness failure]
  next_decision: continue, expand or change

context.title: From objective to investment
context.summary: The churn objective changes the product decision only because ownership, demand and investment are explicit.

panels.label: Decision record
panels.code:
objective: reduce annual churn
use_case: identify 30-day churn risk
portfolio_decision: extend Customer 360
accountable_owner: Customer Data Products
review_date: six months after adoption

details.label: Rule
details.value: Objective is not a use case or a product

context.title: One connected definition
context.summary: The contract is authoritative, while vocabulary, commitments and relationships provide the surrounding meaning.

panels.label: Artifact boundary
panels.code:
ODPS: product identity and interface
ODPV: material business terms
ODPG: objective, use-case and policy links
ODPC: catalog and portfolio reference
ODPR: repeatable validation workflow

context.title: Declare, execute, evidence
context.summary: The contract is declared once, then operational systems provide catalog, access, release and consumption evidence.

panels.label: Operational hand-off
panels.code:
declare: Customer 360 2.4.0
publish: restricted ODPC reference
provision: Retention Analytics access
validate: ODPR recipe execution
evidence: version, access and workflow records

context.title: Evidence changes the decision
context.summary: The observed state is compared with commitments, then findings and value evidence reach an accountable reviewer.

panels.label: Assurance chain
panels.code:
commitment: completeness >= 98%
observation: 94.7%
status: failed
impact: retention analysts may be affected
response: remediate and review investment

details.label: Separation
details.value: Declared target is not performance evidence

context.title: Score evidence separately
context.summary: A valid contract is necessary evidence, but it cannot prove that a capability is accountable, operational or effective.

panels.label: C12 assessment trace
panels.code:
accountability: service owner named
practice: measurement method documented
evidence: 94.7% observation retained
outcome: remediation and impact reviewed
limiting_dimension: outcome

context.title: Scale after the first review
context.summary: The framework is introduced through a bounded decision path, rather than an estate-wide metadata exercise.

panels.label: First implementation sequence
panels.code:
1. DIRECT: agree objective and product decision
2. DEFINE: publish the smallest usable contract
3. OPERATE: connect catalog, access and workflow
4. ASSURE: collect observation and outcome
5. REVIEW: continue, change or stop

details.label: Initial scope
details.value: One product and registered use case

context.title: Fourteen connected artifacts
context.summary: This example keeps portfolio records, operating evidence and ODPS-family artifacts distinct while tracing one decision end to end.

panels.label: Artifact sequence
panels.code:
objective → use case → decision → contract
→ vocabulary → graph → catalog → access
→ version → workflow → observation
→ controls → adoption → value review

context.title: Regulatory-reporting product
context.summary: Use this scenario to test how purpose, access, lineage, controls and review evidence stay connected for a restricted product.

panels.label: Control path
panels.code:
reporting rule → product contract → purpose-bound access
→ upstream lineage → release approval
→ control execution → retained evidence
→ exception and remediation

details.label: Boundary
details.value: Contract alone does not prove compliance

context.title: Governed agent decision path
context.summary: The agent reads structured context, checks purpose and evidence, then stops when a human decision or missing evidence requires escalation.

panels.label: Permitted agent path
panels.code:
discover → read contract → resolve vocabulary
→ traverse allowed graph → check access
→ verify version and assurance evidence
→ execute permitted workflow or escalate

panels.label: Stop conditions
panels.code:
ambiguous vocabulary | denied access | stale contract
failed quality | missing relationship
human approval required

details.label: Output
details.value: Products, versions, graph path and checks performed
